_meta.notes: Country-scoped curated nodes; link via relationships during ingest.

910.name: Early Peoples and Iron Age
910.label: Event
910.description: San rock art tradition; Bantu migration; early iron-working and farming communities on the Zimbabwe plateau.

910.name: San Rock Art Tradition
910.label: Event
910.description: Extensive San rock art across Zimbabwe; Matobo Hills UNESCO site; hunter-gatherer cultural record.

910.name: Bantu Migration and Iron Age
910.label: Event
910.description: Bantu-speaking peoples arrive; Gokomere-Ziwa pottery tradition; iron smelting; cattle-keeping; early farming villages.

920.name: Great Zimbabwe and Successor States
920.label: Event
920.description: Rise and fall of Great Zimbabwe; Mutapa Empire; Rozvi Confederacy; gold trade with Swahili coast.

920.name: Mapungubwe and Precursors
920.label: Event
920.description: Mapungubwe as precursor state; Leopard's Kopje culture; gold and ivory trade; social stratification develops.

920.name: Great Zimbabwe City
920.label: Event
920.description: Great Zimbabwe as capital of a vast trading state; stone-walled Great Enclosure; population 18,000+; gold export via Sofala.

930.name: Mfecane and Ndebele State
930.label: Event
930.description: Mfecane disruptions; Mzilikazi and the Ndebele migrate north; Ndebele Kingdom established in Matabeleland; Lobengula.

930.name: Ndebele Migration under Mzilikazi
930.label: Event
930.description: Mzilikazi leads Ndebele north from Zulu kingdom; defeats Rozvi; establishes powerful Ndebele state in Matabeleland.

930.name: Lobengula and Concession Hunters
930.label: Event
930.description: King Lobengula navigates European concession hunters; Rudd Concession 1888; manipulation by Cecil Rhodes' agents.

940.name: BSAC and Southern Rhodesia
940.label: Event
940.description: Cecil Rhodes' BSAC; Pioneer Column; First and Second Chimurenga; responsible government; settler state; land dispossession.

940.name: Pioneer Column and BSAC Rule
940.label: Event
940.description: Pioneer Column raises British flag at Fort Salisbury 1890; BSAC administers territory; Matabeleland conquest 1893.

940.name: First Chimurenga (Ndebele-Shona Uprising)
940.label: Event
940.description: Combined Ndebele and Shona uprising against BSAC rule; Mlimo spirit medium; Rhodes negotiates peace in Matopos.

950.name: UDI and Liberation War (Second Chimurenga)
950.label: Event
950.description: Ian Smith's Unilateral Declaration of Independence; Rhodesian Bush War; ZANLA and ZIPRA guerrilla campaigns; Lancaster House Agreement; independence.

950.name: Unilateral Declaration of Independence
950.label: Event
950.description: Ian Smith declares UDI 11 November 1965; white minority regime; international sanctions; no independence before majority rule (NIBMAR).

950.name: Second Chimurenga (Bush War)
950.label: Event
950.description: ZANLA (Mugabe) and ZIPRA (Nkomo) wage guerrilla liberation war; Rhodesian counter-insurgency; cross-border raids into Mozambique and Zambia.

960.name: Mugabe Era
960.label: Event
960.description: Early reconciliation; Gukurahundi massacres; one-party tendencies; land reform; economic collapse; hyperinflation; Mugabe ousted.

960.name: Reconciliation and Early Years
960.label: Event
960.description: Mugabe's initial reconciliation policy; education and health expansion; Lancaster House land compromise.

960.name: Gukurahundi Massacres
960.label: Event
960.description: Fifth Brigade massacres of Ndebele civilians in Matabeleland; estimated 20,000 killed; Unity Accord 1987 absorbs ZAPU.

960.name: Post-Mugabe Zimbabwe
960.label: Event
960.description: Military intervention removes Mugabe; Mnangagwa 'new dispensation'; economic continuity; political repression; re-engagement efforts.

960.name: Mugabe Ousted
960.label: Event
960.description: Military intervention November 2017; Mugabe resigns after 37 years; Emmerson Mnangagwa assumes presidency.

960.name: Mnangagwa Governance
960.label: Event
960.description: Disputed 2018 and 2023 elections; economic stagnation; currency crises; diaspora remittances; limited reform.
